Broadwindsor sits in the hills a few miles inland from Bridport and Lyme Regis,
on the Dorset coast, and West Country ships had worked the Newfoundland fishery and the New England trade for more
than a century. Thomas Hutchins, born in Dorset in 1693, crossed sometime after 1712;
why he went is not recorded. Many young West Country men made the same voyage, as seamen or fishermen,
or as servants bound for a few years in return for their passage.
Salem was a busy fishing and shipping town, sending dried cod to Spain, Portugal and the West Indies;
the witch trials were a generation past.
In January 1720 Thomas married Sarah Southwick, of an old Salem Quaker family.
In 1730 he took his family inland to Dudley, in the hill country of Worcester County,
as New England families did once the coastal farms had been divided as far as they would go.
There Thomas the younger was chosen the town’s hog reeve for the west end in 1742,
and in 1744 he married Abigail Pierce at Oxford.
